reports.title: Cloudflare Announces Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

guidance.heading: Financial Outlook
section: For the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, we expect:
•Non-GAAP income from operations of $156.0 to $157.0 million
•Non-GAAP net income per share of $0.43, utilizing weighted average common shares outstanding of approximately 379 million

desk.headline: Revenue up 39% to $782.5m, fastest growth in nearly four years, beat; full-year outlook raised and Q4 guide above estimates
results: Revenue rose 39% to $782.5m, well above the $739.7m estimate, and passed a $3bn annual run rate.
Non-GAAP EPS was $0.38 versus $0.27 a year ago and a $0.34 estimate; on a GAAP basis the net loss widened to $34.1m ($0.10 a share).
Non-GAAP operating margin improved to 17.5%, though gross margin fell to 72.4% from 75.3%.
Operating cash flow was $215.4m and free cash flow $82.1m (10% of revenue) as equipment spending rose; cash and securities totalled $5.13bn.
Current remaining performance obligations (contracted revenue due within a year) grew 37%. Christian Smith was named President of Revenue.

guidance.summary: Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was lifted to $2,963–2,964m and non-GAAP EPS to $1.35. Q4 guidance of $845–846m revenue and $0.43 EPS is above analyst estimates, as reported.

points: The CFO said the company expects to turn a GAAP profit in Q4, well ahead of its earlier target of no later than 2028.
Large-customer momentum: 308 large customers added in the quarter, and those paying over $100k now make up 75% of revenue.
Total contracted revenue (RPO) was $2.88bn, up 34%; customers are using up prepaid contracts faster and renewing early.
CEO Matthew Prince stressed AI agents as a growth driver; developers on the platform grew from 7m to over 10m in the quarter.
Network capex was 15% of revenue, with the full-year expectation unchanged at 14–15%.
call.source: Call transcript: TradingKey, 6 Nov 2026; guidance comparisons from BigGo Finance, 5 Nov 2026

watch: Whether Q4 delivers the first GAAP profit as guided.
Gross margin, which fell about 3 points as network spending rose.
Sales execution under the new President of Revenue.
